questions.question: "Sunrise Industries” are industries __________.

options.text: which are well developed and have ample scope for further development
which improve export performance of the country
which have high growth potential and meet further requirements of the economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**which have high growth potential and meets further requirements of the economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __Concept:__

__
 
• Industries are classified in a number of ways.
 
• They can be primary, secondary, tertiary or quaternary depending on the type of raw material used.
 
• On the basis of size, capital investment, and labour force employed, industries are classified as large, medium, small-scale, and cottage industries.
 
• On the basis of ownership, industries are categorized as (i) public sector, (ii) private sector, and (iii) joint and cooperative sector.

Explanation:__

Sunrise industry:

 
• "Sunrise Industries” are those industries that are new but are growing at a faster pace and are expected to become important in the future. 
 
• These have high growth potential and meet further requirements of the economy. 
 
• For example - food processing industries, petrochemical industry, space tourism, hydrogen fuel production, etc
 
• Sunrise industries are also known as ‘Emerging Industries.
 
• These include Information technology, Wellness, Hospitality, and Knowledge
 
• 'Sunrise industries' is a colloquial term for a sector or business that is in its infancy, but is growing at a rapid pace.
 
• A sunrise industry is typically characterized by high growth rates, numerous start-ups, and an abundance of venture capital funding.
 
• A sunrise industry is often characterized by a high degree of innovation, and its rapid emergence may threaten to push into obsolescence a competing industry sector that is already in decline.

questions.question: Thunder cloud happens in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Troposphere

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Troposphere**

__
 
• Thundercloud happens in **Troposphere**.
 
• The troposphere is the **lowermost layer of the Earth’s atmosphere**. It is the place where nearly all sorts of weather conditions take place, except large storms like hurricanes and large thunderstorms. 
 
• It contains** 99% of the water vapor in the atmosphere.**
 
• The uneven heating of the regions of the troposphere by the sun causes convection currents, and large-scale patterns of winds that move heat and moisture around the globe. 
 
• **The** **temperature in this layer decreases at the rate of 1°C for every 165m of height.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Ionosphere**

__
 
• The ionosphere is an abundant layer of electrons and ionized atoms and molecules that stretches from about 48 km.
 
• The ionosphere is a critical link in the chain of Sun-Earth interactions.
 
• This region is what makes radio communications possible.
 
• If the radio frequency is between 2 MHz to 30 MHz, then it can be communicated via skywave by ionosphere reflection of a wave toward earth.
 
• This type of propagation is used by short-wave broadcast services.
 
• Ionosphere acts as a reflecting surface for this propagation.
 
• It extends its height from 65 to 400 km above the earth's surface.

**Stratosphere**

 
• The atmosphere consists of different layers with varying densities and temperatures.
 
• The stratosphere__ is the second-lowest layer of the earth's atmosphere.
 
• The stratosphere is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• The stratosphere of the atmosphere is also called the ozonosphere.
 
• The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere.
 
• The stratosphere absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from intense, and harmful forms of energy.
 
• Jet airplanes fly through the stratosphere.
 
• The temperature increases with altitude in the stratosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate from Amarkantak Plateau or nearby places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Godavari is the second longest river after the river Ganga. It originates from Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra.
 
• The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry (Yanam).
 
• The other names for the Godavari River are The Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• Godavari river drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Godavari river originates from Bramhagiri mountains at Trimbakeshwar.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner, and the Sabri.
 
• The longest tributary- The Manjira
 
• The largest tributary- The Pranhita
 
• Amarkantak is a place situated in Madhya Pradesh where the rivers Narmada, Johila, and Son emerge. It is also the place where the Satpura and Vindhya ranges meet the Maikal Hills. River Tawa is one of the tributaries of the river Narmada.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Narmada**

 
• The Narmada River flows through various states and finally drains into the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.
 
• The Source of the Narmada is Narmada Kund which is located at Amarkantak in Anuppur District.
 
• Narmada River is the third-longest river that flows entirely within India after the Godavari and the Krishna. 
 
• The length of the Narmada River is 1312 km with a coverage area of 98,796 sq. km.
 
• Narmada River has numerous waterfalls, mainly the Dhuandhar Falls in Jabalpur district.
 
• The Tawa River is the biggest tributary of the Narmada River other than Sher, Shakkar, and Dudhi.
 
• It is one of only three major rivers in peninsular India that run from east to west, along with the Tapti River and the Mahi River.
 
• The major Hydro Power Project in the basin is Indira Sagar, Sardar Sarovar, Omkareshwar, Bargi & Maheshwar.

**Tawa**

 
• The Tawa River is a tributary of the Narmada River of Central India.
 
• The Tawa is the Narmada's largest tributary, at 172 km.
 
• It rises in the Satpura Range of Betul and flowing north and west, joins the Narmada at the village of Bandra Bhan in the Hoshangabad District.
 
• In 1958, construction began on Tawa Dam, which was completed in 1978 in Tawa Nagar to create Tawa Reservoir in the southern Hoshangabad District.

**Son**

 
• Son River is a perennial river located in central India.
 
• It originates near Amarkantak Hill in the Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi district of Chhattisgarh and finally merges with the Ganges River near Patna in Bihar.
 
• Sone river is the second-largest southern tributary of the Ganges' after the Yamuna River.

questions.question: Which of the following leaders formed 'India Home Rule Society'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shyamji Krishna Varma**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shyamji Krishna Varma** was the founder of the **India Home Rule Society**, an organization founded in **1905** in **London** to promote the cause of self-rule in British India. 
 
• He then established India House in Highgate (at 65 Cromwell Avenue) in the same year (July 1905), as a hostel for Indian students, which became a meeting place for Indian revolutionaries in London.
 
• After Krishna Varma's shift to Paris in 1907, the society gave way to the secret nationalist society of **Abhinav Bharat Mandal which was founded by V. D. Savarkar.**
 
• Many prominent Indian nationalists such as **S.R. Rana, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Bhikaji Cama supported the organization. **
 
• Shyamji Krishna Varma was an Indian patriot, a revolutionary fighter, journalist, and lawyer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Annie Besant**

 
• She was a social reformer, theosophist, and Indian independence leader.
 
• Annie Besant was born in Britain and arrived in India in 1893
 
• Annie Besant was the second President of The Theosophical Society from 1907 to 1933.
 
• She was elected President of the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta session in 1917.
 
• She started the Young Men’s Indian Association in 1914.
 
• Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras.

Lala Hardayal

 
• ​He was an Indian nationalist and revolutionary freedom fighter.
 
• He was awarded a scholarship from Oxford University in 1905 and moved to London where in a letter to 'The Indian Sociologist' he depicted his anarchist ideas. He gave up his scholarship and returned to India in 1908. In 1909, he went to Paris and became editor of the Vande Mataram.
 
• Other places visited by him were Algeria, Martinique, Boston, and California.

**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
• He was born on 23rd July 1856 in Ratnagiri, Maharashtra.
 
• Tilak joined Congress in 1890.
 
• He was opposed to moderate ways and views and had a more radical and aggressive stance against British rule.
 
• He was one of the first advocates of Swaraj or self-rule. He gave the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.”
 
• Along with Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai, he was called the ‘Lal-Bal-Pal’ trio of extremist leaders.

questions.question: What is the national fruit of Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jackfruit**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** national fruit of Bangladesh** is the** jackfruit.**
 
• The climate of Bangladesh adds to the nutritional value of the jackfruit and is perfect for its cultivation.
 
• Jackfruit in Bangladesh is viewed as delicious, sweet, tasty, and juicy, and many Bangladeshis use Jackfruit in their curries and other cuisines.
 
• It is made into a variety of different products, such as **canned fruit, dried fruit, and pulp.**
 
• A typical Jackfruit Tree can bear **an average of 150 pieces of fruit each year,** although some of the more exotic jackfruit tree species are known to produce **as many as 250 to 500 pieces.**
 
• For many consumers, the Tree’s nutritional value rests in its seeds as Jackfruit seeds are extremely high in **Vitamin B1 and Vitamin B2.**
 
• The seeds also have very high starch content but are quite low in the presence of iron and calcium.
 
• Each fruit can contain between **100 to 500 seeds**, which are oily to the touch.
 
• With so many uses, **low cost, and high nutritional value**, it is no surprise that jackfruit is the national fruit of Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mango** is the national fruit of India

questions.question: Which of the following is a CORRECT statement?

options.text: Both compounds and elements are pure substance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Both compounds and elements are pure substances.**__

**__Explanation:__**

Matter can be classified into two categories:-

 
• Pure substances - A pure substance does not have any other substance or impurity present and cannot be separated into other kinds of matter by physical processes. 

 
 
• It has a definite set of properties such as boiling point, melting point, density, etc.
 
• A pure substance is composed of one type of atom or molecule.
 
• Ice, iron, hydrochloric acid, calcium oxide, and mercury are pure substances as they have definite compositions.
 
 
 
• Pure substances are classified into two categories:-
 
 
• Elements- A pure substance with only one kind of atom and cannot be broken into two or simpler substances by physical or chemical means is an element.
 
• Compounds- A pure substance composed of two or more elements and chemically combined in a fixed proportion is called a compound.

questions.question: Electrons can be deflected by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ​__Both magnetic and electric fields__**.

**Electrons can be deflected by Both magnetic and electric fields.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **force produced **by the** electric field** is independent of the **electron's speed or direction,** and it is proportional to and in the** direction of the field.**
 
• The** magnetic field's force** is proportional to the field, at a **right angle** to it, and proportionate to the **electron's velocity, **also at a right angle to it.
 
• In the end, this means that an** electron's path** in a uniform **electric field** is a** parabola **and its path in a** uniform magnetic field** is a **helix. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Field:**

 
 
• An electric field is a **physical field **that surrounds **electrically charged particles** and acts as an** attractor or repellent** to all other charged particles in the vicinity.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• The magnetic influence on moving **electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials** is described by a magnetic field, which is a vector field.

questions.question: By which process the cells of the meristematic tissue take up a permanent shape, size, and a function?
questions.solution:
The Corre answer is __Differentiation.__

__**Explanation:**__

Differentiation

 
• A permanent tissue is made up of mature, living, or dead cells divided from meristematic tissues. 
 
• In plants, meristematic tissue loses its ability to divide. After they take up a specific role.
 
• This process of taking up a permanent shape, size, and function of a meristematic tissue into a permanent tissue is called differentiation.
 
• The differentiation process causes the development of various types of permanent tissues
 
• Differentiation is the process in which cells of the root and the shoot apical meristems and the cambium mature to perform specific functions. In this process, lots of structural changes occur within the plant cell.
 
• For instance, The protoplasm is lost during the formation of tracheary elements.
 
• There are two types of Differentiation processes:
 
 
• Dedifferentiation process:
 
 
• In this process, the cells that have lost the capability to divide regain their dividing property under certain conditions.
 
• For instance, the formation of meristems from fully differentiated parenchymal cells. Dedifferentiation of normal cells in the human body leads to the formation of tumour cells.
 
 
 
• Redifferentiation process:
 
 
• Process in which differentiated cells that have lost their ability to divide are reformed from dedifferentiated cells and have the ability to perform specific functions.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Demarcation **is the action of fixing the limits of something. 
 
• ** Simplification:** is the process by which things are made less complicated so that they can be either done or understood

questions.question: A Sonar of a ship sends sound waves of speed 1500 m/s. These waves are reflected back by the ocean floor in 5 seconds. Find the depth (in m) of the ocean floor.
questions.solution:
Given:-

Speed of sound waves = 1500m/s

Total time (time to go + time to come back) of waves = 5sec (2.5 each)

Thus, depth (distance) of the ocean floor = speed × time

= 1500 × 2.5 = 3750m

**EXPLANATION**__:

questions.question: Living things constitute the biotic component of the ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Biosphere.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• The biosphere is the global ecological system integrating all living beings and their relationships, including their interaction with the elements of the lithosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.
 
• **Living things constitute the biotic component of the biosphere**.
 
• The lithosphere consists of the earth's crust and upper part of its mantle.
 
• The atmosphere is what we call 'the air,' or the mixture of gases held around the earth by its gravitational pull.
 
• The hydrosphere is the total sum of all of earth's water in any form, whether it's on the ground as liquid or ice, or in the clouds as water vapour.
 
• The biosphere is the fourth sphere and consists of the places where life can be found. Since life exists in the air, on and in the earth, and on and in water, the biosphere overlaps, connects, and influences all the other spheres - and they all affect the biosphere.
 
• **The mesosphere** and thermosphere are the layers of the atmosphere of the Earth.
 
• **The heliosphere **is a bubble-like region in space which is dominated by the Sun and extends far beyond the orbit of Pluto.

questions.question:
Which of the statements given below are correct?

A. Alexander Zverev won the Tennis 2017 Italian Open Men's Singles.

B. In 2017 Pro Kabaddi League, Selvamani K played for Puneri Paltan.

C. United States hosted the Tennis 2017 Hopman Cup.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alexander Zverev**

 
 
• He plays professional** tennis** for Germany.
 
• The Association of Tennis Professionals has ranked him No. 3 in the world and has maintained his position in the top 10 since July** 2017**.
 
• Alexander Zverev won the Tennis 2017 Italian Open Men's Singles. ***(Hence statement A is correct)***
 
• He won in the ATP finals of **2018 **making a record as the youngest winner championship of the decade.
 
• To date, he has won **15 ATP titles** (13 in singles and 2 in doubles).
 
• He finished his first Grand Slam final in the **2020 US Open** as runner-up.
 
• His fans have named him ‘**Sascha**’ as well.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the 2017 Pro Kabaddi League, Selvamani K played for **Jaipur Pink Panthers.** ***(Hence statement B is incorrect) ***
 
• **Australia** hosted the Tennis 2017 Hopman Cup. ***(Hence statement C is incorrect) ***
